nodes.name: Repeat Hydrogen Reduction (Redispersion)
nodes.procedure: Repeat reduction treatment with hydrogen: heating from 23°C to 500°C under H₂ atmosphere, with residence time at 500°C. Process observed between 400-500°C, especially pronounced above 450°C. Multiple cycles lead to redispersion from ~3.5 nm to 1.9 nm average size.

nodes.description: CO₂ hydrogenation catalytic performance - original, 1st, and 2nd repeat reduction treatments
nodes.source_text: Reversible product selectivity is observed on Ni₁₀Ru₄/TiO₂ (Figs. 1d and S7), which can be controlled by the times of repeat reduction treatment. The original Ni₁₀Ru₄/TiO₂ catalysts exhibit methane-dominated selectivity, with 31.18% CO selectivity, while the catalysts show 100% CO selectivity after repeat reduction treatment. However, after the second times repeat reduction treatment, catalysts exhibit a reverse selectivity from CO to CH₄, as high as 93% CH₄

nodes.description: In-situ ETEM observation of redispersion under hydrogen reduction
nodes.source_text: in-situ ETEM experiments are conducted to track the alloy NPs on Ni₁₀Ru₄/TiO₂ catalyst in the temperature window from 23°C to 500°C under a H₂ atmosphere... the redispersion process under the repeated hydrogen reduction treatment occurs during the heating phase, especially between 400 to 500°C

nodes.description: Time-tracking in-situ CO-DRIFTS and XRD during repeated hydrogen reduction
nodes.source_text: time-tracking CO-DRIFTS combined with the XRD on Ni₁₅Ru₆/TiO₂... after repeat reduction by hydrogen for 1h, the Ru sites change obviously... after repeat reduction by hydrogen for 2h, the low coordinated sites finally become dominant

nodes.characterization_summary: Original Ni₁₀Ru₄/TiO₂ shows broad NP size distribution 2-18 nm with average 3.5 nm; after repeated H₂ reduction at 500°C, distribution narrows with average size 1.9 nm and no NPs >3 nm.
nodes.evidence_snippet: With a broad size distribution on the original Ni₁₀Ru₄/TiO₂ (Fig.1a)... the average size significantly reduces to 1.9 nm (Fig. 1b).

nodes.characterization_summary: EDS confirms homogeneous NiRu alloy formation on TiO₂ support for NPs of all sizes before and after repeated H₂ reduction, without phase separation.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The element distribution on each nanoparticle can be characterized by energy dispersive spectroscopy (EDS) (Figs. 1a, S1-2), which shows the homogeneous formation of NiRu alloy NPs on TiO₂ support...

nodes.characterization_summary: Ni(111) peak shifts to lower angle confirming NiRu alloy structure; after repeated H₂ reduction, peaks broaden and nearly disappear indicating elimination of large alloy particles.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The alloy structure in NiRu/TiO₂ catalysts can be further evidenced with XRD by the peak shift of Ni (111) peak... only the diffraction peaks related to Ni metal become broad and almost disappear...

nodes.characterization_summary: Time-tracking in-situ CO-DRIFTS on Ni₁₅Ru₆/TiO₂ shows low-coordinated Ru sites increase after 1-2h H₂ reduction with bridge sites indicating SAA formation; carbonate/bicarbonate species increase indicating TiOₓ overlayer growth.
nodes.evidence_snippet: In CO-DRIFTS, after repeat reduction by hydrogen for 1h, the Ru sites change obviously... low-coordinated Ru sites... increase... the IR peak intensity of carbonate species... dramatically increase...

properties.technique: Diffuse Reflectance Infrared Fourier Transform Spectroscopy

nodes.characterization_summary: In-situ ETEM under H₂ shows NiRu alloy NPs disintegrate from ~25 nm to 2-3 nm via 'tearing effect' between 400-500°C; small NPs (1-2 nm) remain stable.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Here, a subversive 'tearing effect' on the interface of TiO₂-supported NiRu alloy nanoparticles is in-situ discovered by environmental transmission electron microscopy (ETEM) with a dramatic redispersion process...

nodes.characterization_summary: Original catalyst shows NiO-like Ni 2p₃/₂ with satellite; after reduction shows Ni(OH)₂ peaks. Ti 2p FWHM broadens to 1.89 eV indicating TiOₓ defects.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The slightly multiple-split Ni 2p₃/₂ peak with the strong oscillating satellite peak in the original catalyst is attributed to... NiO species, while the one after redispersion shows only Ni(OH)₂ characteristic peaks.

nodes.characterization_summary: In-situ Ni L-edge shifts to higher energy under H₂ indicating increased Ni valence; Ti L-edge shows reduction to TiOₓ (457.5 eV under H₂ vs 457 eV vacuum).
nodes.evidence_snippet: The related peaks in Ni L-edge of catalyst under hydrogen shift to higher energy than the original one... the Ti L-edge features... indicate the reduction of TiO₂ to TiOₓ species...

nodes.characterization_summary: Ni K-edge XANES shows increased Ni valence after repeated reduction; EXAFS shows Ni-O coordination number increases from 1.02 to 2.48, Ni-Ni decreases from 7.05 to 5.00.
nodes.evidence_snippet: After repeat reduction treatment, the coordination number of the Ni-O path increases from 1.02 to 2.48... coordination number of the Ni-Ni path decreases from 7.05 to 5.00...

properties.description: Fourier Transform Radial Distribution Function plot

nodes.characterization_summary: NiRu/SiO₂ shows agglomeration to larger sizes after repeated H₂ reduction at 500°C with sharper metallic peaks, no redispersion.
nodes.evidence_snippet: After repeat reduction by hydrogen at 500°C, XRD results show the alloyed NPs agglomerated as bigger sizes with sharper metallic peaks...

nodes.characterization_summary: Ni/TiO₂ shows no significant change in overall Ni metal sizes after repeated H₂ reduction, neither redispersion nor agglomeration.
nodes.evidence_snippet: As for the Ni/TiO₂, characterized by XRD, there is no significant change in overall Ni metal sizes after repeat reduction...

nodes.characterization_summary: Ru/TiO₂ after repeated H₂ reduction shows significant increase of high-coordinated Ru sites indicating NP size increase.
nodes.evidence_snippet: As for Ru/TiO₂ after repeat reduction, CO-DRIFTS results show the significant increase of high-coordinated Ru sites...

nodes.characterization_summary: H₂-TPD results confirm chemisorbed hydrogen desorption contributing to Ti species reduction under vacuum.
nodes.evidence_snippet: According to the H₂-TPD results (Fig. S21), the reduction of Ti species under vacuum can be attributed to the desorption of chemisorbed hydrogen...
